subtopics.title: Republic Day 2026 Parade and Chronology
subtopics.summary: Republic Day celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas, and conclude on 29 January with the Beating Retreat Ceremony at Vijay Chowk. The main events fall on 26 January, when the Prime Minister pays homage at the Amar Jawan Jyoti and the President unfurls the National Flag at Kartavya Path. The 2026 parade, the 77th Republic Day, showcased Constitutional values through 30 cultural tableaux.
facts: Festivities officially begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas.
23 January marks the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose.
The President delivers the Republic Day Address on the day before Republic Day.
The Prime Minister pays homage at Amar Jawan Jyoti in early morning of 26 January.
The President unfurls the National Flag at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath).
The National Anthem and a 21-gun salute follow the flag unfurling and mark the formal start of the parade.
The President confers Padma and Gallantry Awards in the evening of 26 January.
Celebrations conclude on 29 January at Vijay Chowk with the Beating Retreat Ceremony.
2026 is India's 77th Republic Day; the theme is 150 Years of Vande Mataram.
Top tableaux: Maharashtra, Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala; Chief Guests: Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa.

subtopics.title: Padma and Gallantry Awards
subtopics.summary: Padma Awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and recognise achievements in all fields involving public service. Gallantry Awards honour bravery of armed forces personnel and are announced twice a year. The Padma Awards 2026 conferred 131 honours, and Shubhanshu Shukla received the Ashok Chakra.
facts: Padma Awards 2026 conferred 131 honours in total.
The 2026 Padma list included 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri.
Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
Padma categories in order of rank: Padma Vibhushan, then Padma Bhushan, then Padma Shri.
Gallantry Awards were conferred on 70 Armed Forces personnel.
Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian on the ISS, was honoured with the Ashok Chakra.
Ashok Chakra is India's highest peacetime gallantry award.
Gallantry Awards are announced twice a year, on Republic Day and Independence Day.
Wartime Gallantry was instituted on 26 January 1950; Peacetime Gallantry in 1952.
Gallantry eligibility covers officers of all ranks (Army, Navy, IAF), reserve forces, Territorial Army and nursing services.

subtopics.title: History of Republic Day
subtopics.summary: 26 January was linked to the Poorna Swaraj declaration from the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929. From 1930 to 1947 the day was celebrated as Independence Day or Poorna Swaraj Day. The Constitution, adopted on 26 November 1949, came into effect on 26 January 1950, making India a sovereign democratic republic.
facts: The Lahore Session of INC in December 1929 passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution.
Poorna Swaraj called for total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule.
The Declaration of Independence was officially promulgated on 26 January 1930.
From 1930 to 1947, 26 January was celebrated as Independence Day or Poorna Swaraj Day.
The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.
The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.
The Constitution repealed the Indian Independence Act 1947 and the Government of India Act 1935.
India ceased to be a Dominion of the British Crown and became a Sovereign, Democratic Republic.
India gained independence on 15 August 1947.
26 November has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015.

subtopics.title: Unfurling and Hoisting the Flag
subtopics.summary: On Republic Day the President unfurls the Tricolour, while on Independence Day the Prime Minister hoists it. The difference reflects the two events: unfurling renews commitment to Constitutional principles, and hoisting symbolises the rise of a new nation.
facts: On 26 January the President of India, as Head of State, unfurls the Tricolour.
On 15 August the Prime Minister, who heads the Union Government, hoists the National Flag.
On 26 January the flag is folded or rolled and attached to the top of a pole.
The President unveils the flag without pulling it up.
On 15 August the flag is positioned at the bottom of the pole and raised from bottom to top.
Unfurling is a symbolic gesture to renew commitment to the principles of the Constitution.
Unfurling highlights India's shift from a British colony to a Sovereign, Democratic Republic.
Hoisting symbolises the rise of a new nation, patriotism and freedom from colonial rule.

quizzes.passage: Republic Day is celebrated in India on 26 January each year, and its origins lie in the freedom movement. This is the 77th Republic Day, marked in 2026. A session of the Indian National Congress passed a resolution that set out a clear political goal for the country. In the years that followed, Congress asked Indians to observe 26 January as a day of national pride, and the date was marked in this way for many years. The country later gained freedom, which led people to reconsider what the day should mean. The Constitution of India was then adopted by the Constituent Assembly, and it provided a new legal framework for the nation. The date chosen for the Constitution to take effect was 26 January, partly because of its nationalist significance. Because of this link, the day is closely associated with the Constitution. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Today the main celebrations take place at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, where a parade is held. The celebrations conclude with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk, and the day remains a reminder of the journey from colonial rule to a republic.

quizzes.passage: Republic Day is observed on 26 January, and its story is closely tied to India's freedom movement. A session of the Indian National Congress produced a resolution demanding total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule. Congress then asked Indians to treat 26 January as a day of national pride, and the date was used in this way for many years. Freedom eventually arrived, and afterwards people reconsidered what the day should signify. The nation's legal framework was built through the work of the Constituent Assembly, which produced the Constitution of India. That Constitution replaced the earlier legal arrangements of colonial rule, so the country moved from being a Dominion of the Crown to a sovereign, democratic republic. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Today the main celebrations take place at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, where a parade is held. The celebrations end with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk. The 2026 parade showcased 30 cultural tableaux under the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram. The parade showcased Constitutional values, and the day therefore recalls both the long struggle for freedom and the adoption of a constitutional system.

quizzes.passage: India observes two national days with the Tricolour, the National Flag, and each has its own ceremony. Republic Day falls on 26 January and marks the day the Constitution came into effect. Independence Day falls on 15 August and marks the nation's freedom from colonial rule. Although the flag is central to both occasions, the way it is handled differs between them. On Republic Day the flag is handled in a way that symbolically renews the nation's commitment to the principles of the Constitution. On Independence Day the flag is raised, a gesture with its own symbolism. The two ceremonies therefore carry different messages while sharing the same symbol. The main Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path, formerly known as Rajpath, in New Delhi, and the celebrations conclude with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk on 29 January. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. The 2026 celebrations carried the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram, and the parade featured 30 cultural tableaux. Republic Day festivities therefore run from 23 January to 29 January. Together these ceremonies remind citizens of the transition from colonial rule to a republic.

quizzes.passage: The Tricolour, India's National Flag, is central to two national occasions held each year. Republic Day is observed on 26 January, and Independence Day is observed on 15 August. Although the flag is present at both, each ceremony has its own character and its own meaning. The Republic Day ceremony recalls the moment when India's legal system took a new shape and the nation became a sovereign, democratic republic. The Independence Day ceremony marks the end of foreign rule and the arrival of freedom. Both occasions are linked to the flag. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Wreath-laying at Amar Jawan Jyoti takes place in the early morning of 26 January. The Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, and the celebrations conclude on 29 January with the Beating Retreat at Vijay Chowk. The 2026 parade showcased 30 cultural tableaux under the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram, and leading tableaux came from Maharashtra, Jammu and Kashmir, and Kerala. The address to the nation is delivered on the day before Republic Day. The 2026 celebration marks the 77th Republic Day, and the Beating Retreat marks the close of the celebrations.
